claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation with Alex.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and responsibilities for Alex.

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute financially to their upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, and I'm not currently contributing financially to their upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's living situation.

**Who does Alex currently live with, and has Alex been living with someone else for more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with my ex-partner. Yes, they've been living there for quite a while now - definitely more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

You've told me that:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex does not live with you
- You are not making financial contributions to Alex's upkeep
- Alex has been living with your ex-partner for more than 8 weeks

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. You're usually considered responsible for a child if either you live with them OR you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money).

When a child goes to live with someone else, you can usually continue to get Child Benefit for 8 weeks. It can continue for longer if you make contributions to the child's upkeep that are at least equal to the Child Benefit payment amount.

Since Alex has been living with your ex-partner for more than 8 weeks and you're not making financial contributions to their upkeep, you would not be considered responsible for Alex under the Child Benefit rules. Your ex-partner (or whoever Alex lives with) would be the person who could claim Child Benefit for Alex, as they are the one responsible for the child.

**Assessment Complete: You are INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

Based on your circumstances, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex because:

- Alex does not live with you
- You are not making financial contributions to Alex's upkeep
- Alex has been living with your ex-partner for more than 8 weeks

Under the Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. You're considered responsible for a child if you either live with them or contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep (for things like food, clothes, or pocket money).

When a child goes to live with someone else, you can continue receiving Child Benefit for 8 weeks. After that, you can only continue if you're making regular financial contributions to the child's upkeep.

Since you're not living with Alex and not making contributions, the person who Alex lives with (your ex-partner) would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex comes to live with you or you start making regular financial contributions - you could potentially become eligible at that time.
